chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him, 'Is it permissible for anyone to make someone from the Jews, Christians, and Magians swear by their gods?' He said, 'It is not permissible for anyone to make someone swear except by Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'
ai.seo_question: How should oaths be administered to Jews, Christians, and Magians according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential principle that while oaths administered to the People of the Book are valid, they must be sworn by Allah alone rather than by their specific idols or deities. This ruling preserves the monotheistic integrity of the oath, aligning with the Shia scholarly emphasis on Tawhid even in legal interactions with non-Muslims, and prevents the implicit validation of their polytheistic beliefs.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, replied when

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Is it correct for anyone that he should get to swear anyone from the Jews, and the Christians, and the Magians, by their gods?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘No! It is not correct for anyone that he should swear except by Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah, who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

if it is proper to make Jews, Christians and Zoroastrians take an oath by their deities. He (the Imam) said, ’It is not proper for anyone to take oath by anything other than Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious.’”
